newsitem.title: UK: Crude palm under pressure at Euro veg oil close.
newsitem.headline: Crude palm under pressure at Euro veg oil close.

text.p: Talk that Egypt had passed at its tender for palm oil on Wednesday and trader scepticism over the PORLA figures released earlier put crude palm oil prices under pressure at the close of the European vegetable oil market.
Egypt opened sealed bids to supply 30,000 tonnes of vegetable oil for delivery in March on Wednesday.

These comprised 10,000 tonnes of palm oil for arrival in first half March, 10,000 tonnes of extra fancy tallow and or bleachable tallow for arrival in second half March and 10,000 tonnes of palm stearin for arrival in first half March.
The Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) put end-December stocks at 792,687 tonnes against 955,958 at end-November.
Production was put at 637,865 tonnes, down from November's 762,539, while exports were seen at 637,899 against 636,554.
Traders said the data seemed to be bullish with lower than expected stocks, but added that this seemed to be due more to a very high local disappearance rate than exports.
"There is a big question mark hanging over the local disappearence rate..." said a trader.
Traders said the local palm oil disappearance was in the region of 163,000 tonnes during December, against 124,000 tonnes in November and 98,000 tonnes during October.
"The 163,000 tonnes seems very high against the previous months' figures which makes us think there will be a revision next month," said another trader.
News that China has cut its import duty on finished palm oil to 12 percent from 18 percent, back-dated to January 1, 1997, boosted early prices. But the rally soon fizzled out.
At the close of business crude palm oil cif Europe was $7.50 down while products were $2.50 to $5 lower with no further business reported.
Coconut finished $15 to $5 lower after afloat traded at $787.50 and Feb/Mar at $760 a tonne cif.
Dec/Jan traded at $772.50 in a switch with Jan/Feb at $765 a tonne.
Soft oils finished with soy oil 0.25 to one guilders lower after May/Jul traded at 97.50 guilders.
Rape oil closed 0.50 guilders down, but traders said sellers would come lower if pushed.

"The market is 0.50 guilders down, but sellers may come another 0.50 guilder lower, however they are a bit nervous of coming out and saying this because although Chicago soy oil is down beans are up," said a trader.
Rape oil's premium over soy oil, based on sellers' prices, was 1.50 guilders to par at the close against 1.50 to 0.75 on Tuesday.
